## Overview

Three deals involving AI coding tools were announced on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, and the reports describe three different sets of terms for existing users. Meta acquired Conductor, whose cloud service [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/04/meta-acquires-ai-coding-startup-conductor-whose-app-runs-several-coding-agents-at-once/) reported goes read-only on November 13 and shuts down on November 20. editor_notes.content_quality: Analysis, 1,497 words by the script count (range 800-2000). It examines a topic, what existing users are told when AI coding-tool startups are acquired, across three same-day deals (Meta-Conductor, Factory-HumanLayer, OpenAI-Pierre) plus one precedent (Stainless, May 2026 and the Google and Cloudflare responses), on four stated dimensions (dated shutdown, refunds, self-hosting, price). Reported facts (Current situation, Comparison) are separated from analysis (Implications), which is labelled 'not a Herald forecast' and stays within what the sources say; the tabulation is labelled 'the Herald's own' and holds row by row. A closing section states what the sources do not establish. Weakness: the Implications section is thin and largely restates reported terms; the analytical value is the side-by-side comparison and the Stainless precedent, which is adequate for an Analysis but not strong. Overlap: the Herald's 2026-11-06 article on orchestration layers covers the Conductor deal as one of four moves (including its shutdown dates) and mentions the Pierre deal only in passing via The Register; this article is limited to user terms and adds HumanLayer, Pierre and the Stainless precedent, so it is distinct, not a duplicate. PR #2832 (News on OpenAI-Pierre, not yet reviewed) will cover one deal; this article uses Pierre as one of three comparison rows.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 10 sources read from raw text; sha256 of every stored snapshot re-verified after decompression against manifest.json (all match). No suspicious_patterns on any source. source-0 SiliconANGLE Conductor: confirms terms not disclosed, own subscriptions and keys, 100,000 users, ordered wind-down (sign-ups stopped Nov 4, Pro features free, cloud read-only Nov 13, shut Nov 20, then deletion; export or move workspaces; refunds for active subscribers; local app works until early 2027, then no new models or critical fixes and Conductor deletes the app's user data), Ona in June. It does NOT say the local app 'shuts down' (see correction 3). source-1 TechCrunch: 'something new' / 'early next year' verbatim (Holtz), Meta confirmed without detail, cloud shuts Nov 20. source-2 InfoWorld Conductor: read-only Nov 13, shut Nov 20, transfer or export, 'It remains unclear whether the new interface planned for early 2027 will support the AI coding tools they currently use.' verbatim, no financial terms disclosed; it is InfoWorld (not SiliconANGLE) that says data is deleted 'when the application shuts down'. source-3 The Register: Holtz blog post, Nov 13/20, 'top model makers have been purchasing innovation (and talent) while they are still flush with investor funds.' verbatim, 'Anthropic's most recent developer tools deal involved Stainless back in May', Pierre and Ona, no price. source-4 The New Stack (HumanLayer): the pipeline snapshot failed (HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge). Route used: live fetch with a Safari User-Agent (curl), HTTP 200, 1,229,556 bytes, sha256 f86a53c02d11b649460d1433a11f2eaf4bf23387909ddd477e690b822fd104e7 (raw HTML read; Archive.org availability API returned no capture, so no archive route). Confirms: published Nov 5, 2026 (3:02pm on the page; 20:02 UTC per the page metadata), 'Announced Wednesday' (= Nov 4), third acquisition in less than a month (Mentlio Oct 9, Typedef Oct 30), no price for any of the three, 'also be refunding paying customers for the last several months' (founders' announcement), 'neither company has set a shutdown date for HumanLayer's hosted service or said which features will carry over', Apache 2.0 on Oct 23 with the third-party API key caveat and self-hosting burden, 'over the coming weeks' (TNS's wording), 'pushing the companies building them to consolidate fast' verbatim, 'HumanLayer users still don't know whether the hosted service will continue beyond the transition, what they'll pay if they move to Factory, or which features they'll be able to keep'. It also carries the line 'TNS owner Insight Partners is an investor in: Factory.' (see correction 2). The article's absence claim is scoped to the cited reports ('reported no shutdown date', 'in the cited reports') and does not assert that no transition period exists; TNS itself refers to 'the transition' without a length. HumanLayer's and Factory's own posts are not cited and were not used to verify; the orchestrator's note that HumanLayer's post gives a transition 'of at least 30 days' could not be confirmed from any cited source and the article does not contradict it. source-5 InfoWorld Pierre: Code.Storage customers can continue until features are brought into Codex, open-source projects remain open, price not disclosed by either company. source-6 SiliconANGLE Pierre: 'plans to acquire' (announced plans to acquire), terms not disclosed, Trees and Diffs underpin Codex's interface, open-source licence continues after closing, plans to integrate the paid hosting service's features into Codex; no refunds, no dates. source-7 openai.com: the pipeline snapshot is a full direct HTTP 200 capture (345,268 bytes, sha256 bad6d673a0186ed157dbb81fe9936603799cf25328e41374be34dfe8d978d495), not a bot-check page; the writer's Archive.org route was not needed for this review. Dated Nov 4, 2026; both quoted sentences verbatim ('Pierre’s open-source projects will remain open-source, and we’ll continue to contribute to them.' and 'Customers can continue using Code Storage after the acquisition closes while we work to bring its features and functionality into Codex.'); closing subject to customary closing conditions including regulatory approvals; separate companies until closing. source-8 The New Stack (Forge/Stainless): stored snapshot is an Archive.org capture of 2026-10-20 (sha256 02de0aabd3437d30311533ccc9d4d31a3a5abb92e23e7d566cdfcb71cb1f6efd; original returned 200); confirms Anthropic acquired Stainless May 18 then Stainless said it would wind down its products including the SDK generator; OpenAI, Google and Cloudflare among affected customers, kept already generated SDKs, lost the shared regeneration service; 'goes some way toward explaining why Cloudflare is making Forge open source' verbatim; Cloudflare 'doesn't name it specifically'; 'None of them solved this problem for us, and some have shut down entirely.' verbatim; 'Within 11 days' observation; Forge Apache 2.0; Google/Speakeasy AGPLv3. source-9 Google Developers Blog: datePublished 2026-09-17; 'In May 2026, right as we were gearing up for Google I/O ... abruptly announced its shutdown.' and 'proprietary, closed-source generators create unacceptable platform risk.' verbatim; Stainless is not named; Speakeasy suite open-sourced under AGPLv3. All 12 quoted strings plus 'plans to acquire' were found verbatim in their sources. Anthropic acquisition of Stainless: stated by The New Stack (Forge article, May 18) and The Register ('Anthropic's most recent developer tools deal involved Stainless back in May'); the article attributes it ('which it said Anthropic acquired on May 18'). The Cloudflare-Stainless link is presented as The New Stack's reading and Cloudflare's own text is quoted without Stainless named, so the flaw recorded in the corrections record on the Herald's 2026-09-30 Forge article (link attributed only to a headline; timing omitted) is not repeated in the body; the summary and Overview phrasing 'after a hosted service closed' do not carry that attribution (correction 1). Allowlist: infoworld.com, theregister.com, siliconangle.com, techcrunch.com, thenewstack.io, developers.googleblog.com and openai.com are all on config/source_allowlist.txt; no additions needed. Independent-source recount, per outlet: SiliconANGLE (2 articles = 1 outlet; independent; Conductor and Pierre pieces largely relay company announcements), TechCrunch (independent; largely relays Conductor's blog post and Axios), InfoWorld (2 articles = 1 outlet; independent; Conductor piece adds Omdia and Pareekh Consulting analysts), The Register (independent; adds its own commentary), The New Stack (independent of Meta, OpenAI, Google, Cloudflare and Anthropic; but its HumanLayer piece discloses that its owner Insight Partners is an investor in Factory, so for the HumanLayer section it counts only with that caveat). Not counted: openai.com (the subject's own announcement) and the Google Developers Blog (a Stainless customer's own blog, an institutional blog not a news outlet; the article labels it a customer's blog). Result: 4 outlets clearly independent plus The New Stack with caveat = 5 outlets by the writer's count, 4 to 5 by mine; requirement of at least 4 sources with at least 2 independent is met (10 sources from 7 distinct publishers: five outlets plus openai.com and the Google Developers Blog). Anthropic disclosure: not required by the policy triggers (Anthropic is named only incidentally as the acquirer of the Stainless precedent and in The Register's list; not in headline, summary or lead; not an Anthropic-product subject or credit line), but the article carries the one-sentence disclosure anyway; it is accurate (contributor_model is Claude Sonnet 5.5, built by Anthropic), neutral, and sits in the closing section; all statements about Anthropic are attributed to The New Stack or The Register.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Three user-terms claims verified: Conductor cloud read-only Nov 13 and shut Nov 20 (SiliconANGLE, InfoWorld, The Register state both dates; TechCrunch states Nov 20; Holtz's blog post is the origin per The Register and InfoWorld; the article attributes the dates to SiliconANGLE, which does state them). HumanLayer: core software Apache 2.0 since Oct 23, no shutdown date per The New Stack. Pierre: not closed when announced (OpenAI: 'Until closing, OpenAI and Pierre will remain separate and independent companies'; SiliconANGLE 'plans to acquire'), Code Storage customers keep the product until features move into Codex (InfoWorld; OpenAI says 'after the acquisition closes while we work to bring its features and functionality into Codex'). Quantifier and absence sentences checked against all 10 sources: 'only Conductor Cloud has shutdown dates in the cited reports' holds (no date for HumanLayer in TNS or for Code Storage in InfoWorld, SiliconANGLE or OpenAI); 'None of the Pierre coverage ... mentions refunds' holds (zero hits for refund in sources 5, 6, 7; refunds appear only in sources 0 and 4); 'No price was disclosed for any of the three deals' holds row by row (InfoWorld and SiliconANGLE, TNS, InfoWorld and SiliconANGLE; The Register says the same); 'None of the cited reports on the three November deals quotes a customer of the acquired product' holds (quoted speakers are Conductor's CEO, HumanLayer's founders, Factory's CEO, analysts, OpenAI). Dates: Nov 4, 2026 was a Wednesday; the HumanLayer date is derived from The New Stack's Nov 5 article saying 'Announced Wednesday'; no relative dates; the Herald's own earlier articles are linked correctly (/article/2026-11/06-... and /article/2026-09/30-..., both exist). Three subordinate issues, filed as clarification records: the summary's Cloudflare framing, the omitted Insight Partners disclosure, and the 'shuts down' attribution to SiliconANGLE.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout. No predictions presented as the Herald's; the Implications section is explicitly bounded. The inference 'which makes those subscriptions separate from Conductor's own plans' in the Exports paragraph is a mild Herald inference from SiliconANGLE's description (users pay for agents via their own subscriptions and keys while Pro subscribers had Conductor plans), harmless but unlabelled.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. The 2026-11-06 orchestration-layer Analysis uses Conductor as one example of coordination layers; this article compares user terms across three deals and a precedent. HumanLayer and the Stainless/Cloudflare/Google precedent are new to the Herald in this framing (the Forge article of 2026-09-30 is linked, with its existing corrections record honoured).
concerns: Summary and Overview say the Stainless shutdown 'shows what two customers did after a hosted service closed'; for Cloudflare the link to Stainless is The New Stack's reading (Cloudflare never names Stainless, and Forge was released about four months after the May events). The body states this correctly; the summary does not.
The only source for the whole HumanLayer section is The New Stack, whose page discloses that its owner Insight Partners is an investor in Factory; the article does not carry that disclosure.

The Implications section attributes to SiliconANGLE that Conductor 'will delete the local app's user data when it shuts down in early 2027'; SiliconANGLE says local copies keep working until early 2027, when new models and critical bug fixes stop and Conductor deletes the app's user data. 'Shuts down' is InfoWorld's wording.
Headline is 148 characters, just under the 150-character guideline; noted only.

The pipeline snapshot of the HumanLayer source failed (403) and the Forge/Stainless source is an Archive.org capture from 2026-10-20; both were read from raw text by the routes recorded in source_verification.
recommendations: State in the body that The New Stack's owner is an investor in Factory when relying on its HumanLayer report.
Where the Herald's wording follows a single outlet's reading of causation (Cloudflare and Stainless), carry the attribution into the summary as well.
Cite the companies' own announcement pages in future when the allowlist permits, so user terms are not carried by one outlet.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A competent, accurately sourced Analysis with a defined topic, verified quotes, correctly scoped absence claims, a correctly handled Cloudflare/Stainless caveat in the body, and independence met (4 outlets clearly independent plus The New Stack with a disclosed ownership caveat). Three subordinate clarifications are filed; none touches the headline's facts or the lead's central claims, so APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate cross-deal comparison of what users of AI coding tools are told after acquisitions, of interest to a defined developer audience
